name: Flying Colors, green and light green (1979)
description: Braniff International's 'Flying Colors' two-tone scheme in its green and light green pair, as still worn by many 727-200s in 1979: the body Braniff green above a level line just under the windows (about 0.55 m below the centerline, under the nose tip) and light green below it to the belly, the fin, rudder, center engine fairing and tailplane Braniff green. Across the fin's middle a level light green band from the 'BI' aft to the trailing edge, with a large white 'BI' (heavy extended capitals) on it, standing mostly on the S-duct fairing, and 'Flying Colors' in small white lettering ahead of it on the fairing. 'BRANIFF INTERNATIONAL' in white forward-leaning extended capitals over the forward cabin windows, a small US flag ahead of it. Bare polished nacelles, gray wings.

titles.style: Braniff International's 1970s lettering in white: heavy, extended, forward-leaning capitals with square counters and open, flat-topped A's (Harper and George's 'International' face), over the forward cabin windows from just behind the forward door to about the wing, a small US flag ahead of it.

logos.description: A small US flag ahead of the title, the canton forward on each side.

notes: Measured 2026-11-24 for ghost flights. Read on N426BN (September 1977), a dull slide: the green pair's colors are the least certain. The four Flying Colors pairs share one drawing (BI1928/flying-colors-red, -orange, -green, -blue differ only in palette, id, name and notes): when one's drawing changes, change all four. The split is level in meters, 0.55 m below the centerline (N454BN reads -0.49 to -0.17 m and N447BN -0.84 to -0.55 m along the cabin; the two fits disagree by up to 0.3 m, so it's their middle, drawn straight and level, not either photo's tilt). Every straight edge is sampled at the shape's own crown and belly points and pruned to 0.3 mm. The fin's band is level on the aircraft, from 2.87 to 4.43 m above the centerline (N454BN), from the 'BI''s aft letter to the trailing edge. Its lower edge falls on the S-duct's fairing, below the fin's root (4.05 m), where fin paint can only run straight on down (the renderer carries any point at or below the root to the fairing's foot): so it's drawn down to the foot of the fairing, and the strip of the upper color under it (1.3 to 2.87 m, aft of the 'BI') is drawn in the lower color. A renderer that can should stop it 2.87 m up. Its top is drawn at the fin's root (4.05 m; the photo reads 4.43 m), level with the 'BI''s top as the photo shows them, and the 'BI''s middle is set at y -0.30, where the reference renderer draws it as N454BN shows it (photo_trace's probe read -0.11; below the root the two place the fairing's paint differently). it runs aft of the 'BI' on both faces (N431BN and N434BN's right sides). The title's capitals are about 0.45 m tall with their foot about 0.15 m over the windows' tops, from 5.8 m back (the flag) to 18.9 m (N447BN). It leans forward on both sides, as ordinary italics. The tailplane is drawn in the upper color as the photos show it from the side. Registrations (small, white, on the aft body) aren't drawn. Colors are read off slides (Kodachrome and Ektachrome shift them) and are approximate, not Braniff's specification. Alexander Calder painted three Braniff aircraft (the DC-8-62 'Flying Colors of South America', 1973; the 727-200 N408BN 'Flying Colors of the United States', 1975-76; 'Salute to Mexico' was planned but never applied). They're his artwork and aren't drawn here. By late 1979 N408BN had been repainted in Braniff's own colors.

B722.note: The fin's 'BI' and 'Flying Colors' stand mostly on the 727's S-duct fairing under its short T-tail fin, and were measured there alone (N454BN, N447BN). So they're the 727's: on another type the scheme keeps its body title, flag and the fin's band but no fin lettering, which would crowd or run off a fin of another shape.

titles.style: Braniff International's 1970s lettering in white: heavy, extended, forward-leaning capitals with square counters and open, flat-topped A's (Harper and George's 'International' face), over the forward cabin windows from just behind the forward door to about the wing, a small US flag ahead of it.
'Flying Colors' in small white upright sans-serif, capitals and lowercase, on the S-duct fairing ahead of the 'BI'.

logos.description: Braniff International's 'BI' in white: two heavy, extended capitals, square-cornered with small square counters, about 1.55 m tall, standing mostly on the S-duct fairing at the band's forward end. Reads the same way on both sides.
A small US flag ahead of the title, the canton forward on each side.
